key_insight: AI-guided single-cell imaging and label-free enrichment revealed morphological and genomic heterogeneity in metastatic breast cancer cells from malignant effusions.
clinical_relevance: This research approach could enable molecular characterization of accessible metastatic samples, but clinical utility and treatment-selection benefits remain unproven.
method: Applied a pre-trained deep learning model to single-cell brightfield images to estimate tumor cell fractions and characterize morphology.
Used morphology-guided microfluidics for label-free tumor cell enrichment.
Profiled copy-number alterations and mutations, comparing enriched cells with available matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors.
evidence_signal: In 10 patients, imaging identified putative tumor cells across 25 samples (median tumor cell fraction, 5.4%) and four tumor morphotypes; genomic profiling showed shared alterations and divergence across analytes.
watch_item: The small cohort and tumor-fraction-dependent genomic signal warrant broader validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions
